blocks.text: This chapter is part of Elihu’s four uninterrupted speeches, which begin only after Job and the three friends have stopped speaking. Elihu is presented as angry with both sides and as having held back because of his youth. How his role should be understood remains disputed: some readers see him as preparing for the divine answer, while others see him as another inadequate defender of retribution. His absence from the prologue, the divine address to Job, and the epilogue’s rebuke does not by itself settle that question. Elsewhere, Job’s endurance can be understood as persistence through the story and in light of its outcome; it should not be taken to require silent endurance of abuse or to prevent escape and protection.

sections.title: Reading Elihu in the Larger Book
